text: I get stressed out easily and often worry about things that might go wrong in my relationships.
concept_reference: Neuroticism is a strong negative predictor of relationship satisfaction.

text: I follow a schedule and am exacting in my work and commitments.
concept_reference: Conscientiousness predicts long-term relationship satisfaction and stability.

text: I sometimes insult people or hold grudges when I am frustrated.
concept_reference: Agreeableness is positively linked to relationship satisfaction; insulting behavior maps to low agreeableness.

text: I am the life of the party and enjoy being the center of attention.
concept_reference: Extraversion is linked to relationship satisfaction but requires matching or complementarity.

text: I spend a lot of time reflecting on abstract ideas, concepts, and unconventional philosophies.
concept_reference: Openness to experience can both positively and negatively affect relationship satisfaction depending on partner match.

text: Scenario: Your partner is unexpectedly 30 minutes late coming home and hasn't texted. What is your immediate thought process?
options: I assume they got stuck in traffic and wait patiently.
I text them once to check in and find something else to do.
I start worrying that they were in an accident.
I get angry that they are being disrespectful of my time.
concept_reference: High neuroticism correlates with interpreting ambiguous relationship cues negatively.

text: I often worry that my partner will not want to stay with me or that they don't love me enough.
concept_reference: Attachment anxiety is a reliable predictor of relationship dissatisfaction and fear of abandonment.

text: I don't feel comfortable fully opening up and relying on romantic partners.
concept_reference: Attachment avoidance indicates discomfort with closeness, predicting lower relationship quality.

text: I find it relatively easy to get close to others and feel comfortable depending on them.
concept_reference: Secure attachment strongly correlates with long-term stability and constructive conflict management.

text: I rarely worry about being abandoned by my partner.
concept_reference: Reverse-coded item assessing absence of attachment anxiety.

text: When feeling highly stressed, I tend to physically pull away and seek alone time rather than seeking comfort from my partner.
concept_reference: Behavioral manifestation of avoidant attachment in high-stress situations.

text: Scenario: You and your partner have a minor disagreement. Afterwards, your partner asks for an hour of space. What is your immediate impulse?
options: Feel highly anxious and try to force a resolution immediately.
Use the time to distance myself and consider breaking up.
Feel slightly annoyed but respect the boundary.
concept_reference: Scenario measures anxious and avoidant behavioral activation under relationship threat.

text: During a disagreement, it is more important to me to keep the peace than to prove I am right.
concept_reference: Assesses accommodating vs. dominant conflict styles.

text: Scenario: You discover your partner made a medium-sized financial purchase without discussing it. How do you handle it?
options: Bring it up immediately and express my frustration.
Wait until we are both relaxed to calmly ask about it.
Make a sarcastic comment about their spending habits.
Avoid bringing it up to prevent an argument.
concept_reference: Scenario assesses directness and hostility in conflict initiation.

text: I have previously walked out of a room in the middle of a heated argument to cool down.
concept_reference: Behavioral assessment of stonewalling or self-soothing withdrawal.

text: I find it easy to completely let go of negative feelings after a fight is resolved.
concept_reference: Measures lack of grudge-holding, reverse-coded indicator of forgiveness.

text: How important is it that your partner shares your exact approach to resolving arguments?
concept_reference: Assesses need for homophily in conflict management styles.

text: When I am upset, I take time to process my emotions before speaking or acting.
concept_reference: High emotional regulation leads to more constructive interpersonal behavior.

text: In the past month, I have snapped at someone close to me primarily because I was stressed about something else.
concept_reference: Behavioral spillover of stress indicates poor emotional compartmentalization.

text: Scenario: You have had a terrible day at work and come home to a messy house. What is your most likely reaction?
options: Take a deep breath and ask my partner for help cleaning.
Clean it myself but feel quietly resentful.
Lash out at my partner for not maintaining the house.
Ignore the mess and go straight to bed.
concept_reference: Situational assessment of emotional regulation and frustration tolerance.

text: I am able to quickly bounce back and return to baseline after a frustrating event.
concept_reference: Resilience and emotional recovery are positive predictors for relationship satisfaction.

text: My emotions often feel completely out of my control.
concept_reference: Reverse-coded measure of emotional volatility.

text: Rank the following communication methods from most to least preferred for discussing a sensitive relationship topic.
concept_reference: Assesses medium preference for serious relationship discussions.

text: Scenario: Your partner has a habit that mildly annoys you. How do you communicate this to them?
options: Directly tell them it bothers me.
Drop subtle hints and hope they notice.
Make a joke about it to soften the blow.
I don't say anything; it's not worth the conflict.
concept_reference: Measures directness vs. passive-aggressiveness in communication.

text: I regularly ask my partner about their day and actively listen without interrupting.
concept_reference: Behavioral active listening is a core component of perceived partner responsiveness.

text: It is difficult for me to express my needs clearly to a romantic partner.
concept_reference: Reverse-coded measure of expressive communication difficulty.

text: How important is it that your partner is highly verbal and expressive about their feelings?
concept_reference: Assesses compatibility weight for expressive communication styles.

text: Do you require your partner to share your specific religious or spiritual beliefs?
options: Yes, it is a strict requirement
concept_reference: Religious homophily is a strong sorting factor in marital selection.

text: Rank the following in order of priority in your life right now:
concept_reference: Assesses macro-level value alignment.

text: Scenario: You are offered a major career promotion, but it requires moving far away from both of your families. Do you take it?
options: Yes, career advancement is the priority.
No, being close to family is more important.
I would only take it if my partner fully supported the move.
concept_reference: Measures trade-offs between ambition and family proximity.

text: I actively participate in religious, spiritual, or community service events at least once a month.
concept_reference: Behavioral indicator of community/religious involvement.

text: How important is it to you that your partner has a high level of career ambition?
concept_reference: Assesses desired mate value on the status-resources dimension.

text: Potential relationship partners are either inherently compatible or they are not; you cannot force it.
concept_reference: Assesses 'destiny' relationship beliefs, which correlate with lower persistence during conflict.

text: A successful relationship evolves mostly through hard work, compromise, and resolution of incompatibilities.
concept_reference: Assesses 'growth' relationship beliefs, linking to constructive coping mechanisms.

text: Scenario: After 6 months of dating, you and your partner realize you have completely different hobbies and weekend interests. What does this mean?
options: It is a sign we are fundamentally incompatible.
It is a minor hurdle we can overcome by finding new shared interests.
It is perfectly fine; we don't need to do everything together.
concept_reference: Tests practical application of growth vs destiny beliefs in response to discovered dissimilarity.

text: If a relationship requires a lot of effort early on, it probably isn't meant to be.
concept_reference: Reverse-coded item capturing destiny/soulmate ideology.

text: How important is it that your partner believes relationships require constant work and adaptation?
concept_reference: Explicit preference for growth-oriented partners.

text: What is your stance on having children?
options: Have children and do not want more
concept_reference: Fertility and family planning are core compatibility filters in mating markets.

text: Are you seeking a relationship that ultimately leads to marriage?
options: Open to it, but not required
No, I do not want to marry
concept_reference: Relationship trajectory alignment serves as a primary hard constraint.

text: I am currently taking actionable steps (e.g., saving money, studying) towards a specific 5-year life goal.
concept_reference: Behavioral indicator of future-oriented planning and conscientiousness.

text: Scenario: You receive a sudden, unexpected windfall of $50,000. What is your primary use for it?
options: Invest it for retirement or long-term savings.
Use it as a down payment for a house.
Spend it on a luxury vacation or dream experience.
concept_reference: Scenario reveals financial risk tolerance and long-term vs short-term orientation.

text: If my partner wanted to relocate to a different country for their dream job, I would be willing to move with them.
concept_reference: Measures geographic flexibility and willingness to sacrifice for a partner.

text: What is the minimum educational background you require in a potential partner?
concept_reference: Educational assortative mating is heavily documented in online dating behavior.

text: Which of the following best describes your general approach to personal finances?
options: Strict budgeter; save as much as possible.
Moderate saver; I budget but leave room for fun.
Live for today; money is meant to be spent.
concept_reference: Financial compatibility significantly impacts long-term relationship stability.

text: How important is it that your partner earns a similar or higher income than you?
concept_reference: Stated preferences for partner income are strong drivers of mate selection algorithms.

text: I actively track my monthly budget and know exactly where my money goes.
concept_reference: Behavioral measurement of financial conscientiousness.

text: Scenario: You and your partner are planning a two-week vacation. What is your preferred travel style?
options: Mid-range hotels and a mix of paid tours and free exploration.
Budget backpacking, hostels, and street food.
concept_reference: Reveals lifestyle socioeconomic alignment and spending habits.

text: Do you smoke, and are you willing to date a smoker?
options: I smoke & will date a smoker
I smoke & will not date a smoker
I do not smoke & will date a smoker
I do not smoke & will not date a smoker
concept_reference: Smoking is a strict deal-breaker for a significant percentage of online daters.

text: I engage in intentional physical exercise at least three times a week.
concept_reference: Behavioral assessment of fitness lifestyle, often subject to assortative matching.

text: I typically wake up early on weekends to start my day, rather than sleeping in.
concept_reference: Behavioral assessment of circadian rhythms (morningness/eveningness).

text: Rank the following weekend activities from most to least enjoyable for you.
options: Night out at a busy club or bar
Quiet evening at home watching movies
concept_reference: Captures experiential preference clustering relevant for reciprocal recommendation.

text: I prefer my living space to be meticulously organized at all times.
concept_reference: Assesses domestic compatibility and trait conscientiousness.

text: I consume alcohol regularly (e.g., more than 3 times a week).
concept_reference: Substance use homophily is a predictor of long-term compatibility.

text: I prefer to live in the moment rather than planning too far ahead.
concept_reference: Distinguishes present-hedonistic from future-oriented decision making.

text: When making major decisions, I heavily weigh how it will impact my life five to ten years from now.
concept_reference: Future orientation correlates with relationship persistence and stability.

text: Scenario: You have a completely free weekend with no obligations. How do you approach it?
options: I plan a detailed itinerary to maximize the time.
I outline one or two loose ideas but leave room for spontaneity.
I decide completely on the fly as the day unfolds.
concept_reference: Scenario measures structural planning versus spontaneity.

text: I often feel anxious when I think about the future.
concept_reference: Maps future time perspective to neuroticism/anxiety traits.

text: After attending a large social event, I feel energized rather than drained.
concept_reference: Classic metric for extroverted energy recharge.

text: I actively seek out opportunities to meet new people and expand my social circle.
concept_reference: Behavioral indicator of high social energy and openness.

text: I prefer maintaining a few very close, deep friendships over a large network of casual acquaintances.
concept_reference: Identifies depth vs. breadth social preference patterns.

text: Would you consider dating someone whose social energy needs (introversion/extroversion) are the complete opposite of yours?
concept_reference: Measures openness to complementarity vs similarity in personality.

text: How important is it that you and your partner share the exact same level of extroversion?
concept_reference: Explicit weighting for personality homophily.

text: Do you have allergies to or refuse to live with pets (e.g., dogs/cats)?
options: I love pets and want/have them
concept_reference: Pet compatibility serves as a strict environmental deal-breaker.

text: What is the maximum geographic distance you are willing to commute for a relationship?
concept_reference: Proximity is a primary predictor of relationship initiation in online dating.

text: Do you have strict dietary restrictions (e.g., vegan, kosher) that your partner must also follow or accommodate?
options: Yes, my partner must share my diet
Yes, but my partner doesn't have to share it
concept_reference: Lifestyle constraints often operate as hard filters in matching algorithms.

text: Scenario: You discover your partner maintains a close, platonic friendship with their ex. How do you respond?
options: It is a complete deal-breaker; I would end it.
I would be uncomfortable and ask them to limit contact.
I wouldn't mind as long as there are clear boundaries.
I think it's healthy that they are on good terms.
concept_reference: Evaluates boundaries and jealousy triggers, predicting conflict.

text: How important is it that your partner shares your exact political orientation?
concept_reference: Political homophily is increasingly utilized as a deal-breaker in dating markets.

text: I am immediately drawn to someone's physical appearance before evaluating their personality.
concept_reference: Assesses weighting of searchable traits (appearance) vs experiential traits.

text: I typically find myself romantically attracted to someone only after a strong emotional or intellectual bond has formed.
concept_reference: Differentiates primary physical attraction from demisexual/sapiosexual attraction patterns.

text: Scenario: On a first date, the conversation is slightly awkward and stilted, but you find them physically very attractive. Do you go on a second date?
options: Yes, physical attraction is enough to try again.
Maybe, if I think the awkwardness was just nerves.
No, conversational chemistry is mandatory for me.
concept_reference: Tests the tradeoff between physical attractiveness (actor variance) and interaction chemistry (relationship variance).

text: Rank the following in terms of what creates the strongest initial chemistry for you.
concept_reference: Captures heterogeneous ideal partner preferences and attraction drivers.

text: How important is a high degree of sexual compatibility and frequency in a long-term relationship?
concept_reference: Sexual satisfaction is a top relationship-specific predictor of overall relationship quality.
